cards.text: This is the Garden of Eden, friend, where the man and his wife live. Meet the serpent, more crafty than any beast of the field the LORD God had made. He asks the woman, “Did God really say, ‘You must not eat from any tree in the garden?’”

cards.question: The serpent is asking about the trees. True or false: God told the man and woman they could not eat from any tree in the garden.

cards.text: ANY tree? That's like hearing ONE parking spot is reserved and going, “So we can't park ANYWHERE?” The woman sets him straight: they may eat the fruit of the trees.
But about the tree in the middle of the garden, she says God told them not to eat of it or even touch it.

cards.question: About the tree in the middle of the garden, what does the woman say God said would happen if they eat of it?
Now the crafty serpent answers the woman about dying. What does he tell her?

answers.text: You will surely die if you touch it
You will surely die only in old age

cards.text: Then the serpent keeps going. He says God knows that in the day they eat of it, their eyes will be opened.

cards.question: The serpent says that if they eat from the tree, they will be like ___, knowing good and evil.

cards.text: Now the woman sees the tree is good for food, pleasing to the eyes, and desirable for obtaining wisdom. Three for three, friend, and that tree's getting better reviews than my whole bakery.

cards.question: The woman sees all of that in the tree. What does she do next?

answers.text: She takes the fruit and eats it
She walks away from the tree
She asks the serpent to leave

cards.question: The woman gives some of the fruit to her husband. True or false: he was off in another part of the garden when this happened.

cards.text: He was right there with her, and he ate it too. Then the eyes of both of them were opened.

cards.question: The eyes of the man and his wife are opened, and they know that they are ___.

cards.text: So they sew together fig leaves and make coverings for themselves. Their eyes are open, and the first thing on the to-do list is an emergency tailor job.
Then the man and his wife hear the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the breeze of the day.

cards.question: The man and his wife hear the LORD God in the garden. True or false: they hide themselves among the trees of the garden.

cards.text: But the LORD God calls out to the man, “Where are you?” Friend, hiding from the LORD God in the garden is like hiding from your landlord inside the apartment HE owns.

cards.question: The man answers the LORD God from his hiding spot. Why does he say he hid?

answers.text: He was afraid because he was naked
He was ashamed of what the serpent said
He was busy working in the garden

cards.text: The LORD God asks him, “Who told you that you were naked?” Then He asks if the man has eaten from the tree He commanded him not to eat from.

cards.question: The LORD God has asked the man about the tree. True or false: the man says the serpent gave him the fruit.

cards.text: He says, “The woman whom You gave me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.” Friend, that's like telling your boss, “The coworker YOU hired is why my report is late.”
Then the LORD God turns to the woman: “What is this you have done?”

cards.question: The woman answers the LORD God that the ___ deceived her, and she ate.

cards.text: So the LORD God speaks to the serpent: “Because you have done this, cursed are you above all livestock and every beast of the field!”

cards.question: The LORD God tells the serpent that on his ___ he will go, all the days of his life.
True or false: the LORD God also tells the serpent he will eat dust all the days of his life.

cards.text: Then the LORD God says He will put enmity between the serpent and the woman, and between the serpent's seed and her seed.

cards.question: The LORD God tells the serpent that one will crush the other's head. Who crushes whose head?

answers.text: Her seed crushes the serpent's head
The serpent crushes her seed's head
The serpent's seed crushes her head

cards.text: And the serpent will strike his heel. Then to the woman, the LORD God says He will sharply increase her pain in childbirth.

cards.question: True or false: the LORD God also tells the woman her desire will be for her husband, and he will rule over her.

cards.text: Then He turns to the man, Adam. Because Adam listened to the voice of his wife and ate from the tree, cursed is the ground because of him.

cards.question: How does the LORD God tell Adam he will eat of the ground all the days of his life?

cards.text: The ground will yield thorns and thistles, and by the sweat of his brow he'll eat his bread. Working the ground just got switched to HARD MODE.

cards.question: The LORD God says Adam will return to the ground, because out of it he was taken. What does He say Adam is?

cards.text: After all of that, Adam gives his wife a name.

cards.question: Adam names his wife ___.
Why does Adam name his wife Eve?

answers.text: She would be the mother of all the living
She was the first one to see the tree
She would help him work the ground

cards.question: Remember those fig-leaf coverings? What does the LORD God make for Adam and his wife?

cards.text: The LORD God doesn't just make the garments, He clothes them. Fig leaves, you are officially RETIRED.
Then the LORD God says, “Behold, the man has become like one of Us, knowing good and evil.” And He speaks of the man reaching out his hand to take from one more tree.

cards.question: True or false: after this, the LORD God lets the man stay in the Garden of Eden.

cards.text: The LORD God banishes him from the Garden of Eden, to work the ground he was taken from.

cards.question: The LORD God drives the man out. What does He station on the east side of the Garden of Eden?

answers.text: Cherubim and a whirling sword of flame
A pillar of fire and cloud

cards.question: The cherubim and the whirling sword of flame guard the way to the tree of ___.

cards.text: That's the tree the LORD God spoke of, friend: reach out, take, eat, and live forever. Now the way to it is guarded.

findings.problem: The opening card says the Garden of Eden is where the man and his wife live, but it cites only Genesis 3:1. The garden's name doesn't appear until Genesis 3:23-24. The detail that they live there comes from Genesis 2:8, 15, which the card never cites.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "They will lose their names" is silly next to "They will die" and "They will fall asleep." Nothing in the setup makes it believable.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "Only at harvest" is a time, while "Through toil" and "Through trading" are ways of getting food. It also doesn't fit "all the days of his life." The question "How does the LORD God tell Adam..." can also be read as asking how God speaks rather than how Adam will eat.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Card 6 says only that the man might take from "one more tree." It leaves out the rest of Genesis 3:22: take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever. As a result, card 10's blank (life, knowledge or wisdom) can't be reasoned out from the cards and becomes a luck pick. Telling "eat, and live forever" here would set up an informed guess without naming the tree.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The last card goes back to the Genesis 3:22 detail that card 6 held back. It then repeats what cards 9-10 already told: "Now the way to it is guarded." This makes it a recap rather than a card that moves the passage forward.
